title: Describing people: appearance
subtitle: auburn hair, a good figure, stunning
summary: Describe someone's hair, face, complexion, height, build and general appearance - and choose the polite word rather than the blunt one.

lesson.heading: Hair and face
lesson.text: Hair can be **straight**, **wavy** or **curly**, and a man may have a **crew-cut**, a **beard** and a **moustache**. As people get older their hair may start **receding**, or they may go **bald**.

examples.text: She's got long, **wavy** hair and she's **round-faced**.
He's got **receding hair** and a few **wrinkles**.
examples.note: wrinkles = the small lines on an older person's face

examples.text: He used to have black hair but now it's **gone grey**, almost white.

lesson.heading: Face shapes and hair colours
rows: slightly fat, especially of a face
light-coloured hair (fair also works for skin)
dark hair or a dark complexion
red-brown (a compliment): She has such beautiful auburn hair.

lesson.heading: Skin and complexion
lesson.text: Your **complexion** is the natural colour and quality of the skin on your face. **Fair** and **dark** can be used for hair, complexion or skin.

examples.text: Some people like getting a **tan** in summer.
examples.note: a tan = skin that has gone darker in the sun

examples.text: The risks of getting **sunburnt** are well known.
She still has a lovely fresh **complexion**.

lesson.heading: Height and build - choose your word carefully
General appearance
lesson.text: A **smart**, **elegant**, **well-dressed** person looks carefully put together; the opposite is **scruffy**, **untidy-looking** or **messy-looking**.

examples.text: She's a very **smart** and **elegant** woman, always **well-dressed**.
Her husband is quite the opposite, very **scruffy** and **untidy-looking**.
Chloe looked **stunning** in her red dress.
He's very **good-looking**, but his friend's rather **unattractive**.

examples.note: feature = a part of the face

lesson.text: The suffix *-ish* is useful for being vague about people: She's **tallish**. He has **brownish** hair. He must be **thirtyish** (or *in his thirties*).

exercises.prompt: I wish I could get a ___ like yours but my skin just goes red in the sun.
exercises.explanation: Getting a tan = letting your skin go darker in the sun.

exercises.prompt: My cousin used to have a lovely ___ but she's put on weight since she stopped taking exercise.
exercises.explanation: If someone has a nice figure, they have an attractive shape.

exercises.prompt: Thomas's eyes are his best ___ - they're so large and such a deep brown.
exercises.explanation: Your best feature is the most attractive part of your face.

exercises.prompt: Jess is in her thirties but she still has the same lovely fresh ___ as her young daughter.
exercises.explanation: Complexion is the natural colour and quality of the skin on your face.

exercises.prompt: Staff at the bank were told to dress smartly so they would always create a good first ___ on customers.
exercises.explanation: A first impression is someone's first reaction to you.

exercises.prompt: I'd call her ___ rather than ginger-haired - her hair's dark brown with just a tinge of red.
George says that the ___ round his eyes just show that he has smiled a lot in his life.
exercises.explanation: Wrinkles are the small lines that appear on the skin with age.

exercises.prompt: *I thought you said he was the short, chubby one.* Which reply gives the opposite description?
options: No, no, he's the tall, thin-faced one.
No, no, he's the stout, round-faced one.
No, no, he's the plump, stocky one.
No, no, he's the short, well-built one.
exercises.explanation: The opposite of short and chubby is tall and thin-faced.

exercises.prompt: *Was that his brother, the one with wavy hair?* Which reply gives the opposite description?
options: No, completely the opposite, his brother's the straight-haired one.
No, completely the opposite, his brother's the curly-haired one.
No, completely the opposite, his brother's the auburn one.
No, completely the opposite, his brother's the freckled one.
exercises.explanation: Straight hair is the opposite of wavy or curly hair. (Bald would also work.)

exercises.prompt: *She's always quite well-dressed, so I've heard.* Which reply contradicts it?
options: What! Every time I see her, she's scruffy and untidy-looking.
What! Every time I see her, she's smart and elegant.
What! Every time I see her, she's stunning.
What! Every time I see her, she's stocky.
exercises.explanation: Scruffy and untidy-looking are the opposites of well-dressed.

exercises.prompt: Match each description with its more polite or more positive alternative.
Does each word describe hair, build, or general appearance?

exercises.statement: *Ugly* is a neutral word that you can safely use about someone's appearance.
exercises.explanation: Ugly is a very strong word and could be offensive. Say rather plain, rather ordinary or unattractive instead.

exercises.answer: She's a very smart and elegant woman, always well-dressed.
exercises.explanation: Smart, elegant and well-dressed all describe a carefully put-together appearance.
